finding: Taken pattern by pattern: the deprecated two-endpoint event-stream transport is absent and its absence is checked from the wire, every call is a single POST to one endpoint; nothing needs a sticky session - no session identifier appears anywhere in the capability's code, the revision is declared and refused per call rather than negotiated at bind, the catalogue is re-read at every bind and the second server withdraws a tool between two binds without breaking the run, and the local server holds no conversational state, deciding each request on its bearer audience alone; and tool exposure is bounded by a declared surface refused before dispatch rather than left open. So none of the four ruled-out patterns is present as the build's own design. Two things keep it from leading. Authorization is still optional in practice on the path most likely to be used - a static bearer token with no audience binding is what the live adapter falls back to unless the discovery flag is set, and the two swap adapters authenticate nothing at all - and the revision's own additions are not taken up: correlation travels as private x-prefixed headers rather than a declared extension, and the method and name routing headers the revision introduced appear in this repository only as a research note about what a mature build would carry. Nothing demonstrates a server being restarted or replaced mid-turn; statelessness is inferred from the absence of session state rather than shown by killing a server between two round trips.
